key_insight: In perovskite nanocrystal solids, exciton transport is limited more by energetic disorder than by structural polydispersity, especially for longer ligand chains.
engineering_relevance: Ligand length engineering can be used to tune nanocrystal disorder and improve charge/exciton transport in LEDs, lasers, and solar cells.
method: Resolved exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy.
Compared nanocrystal solids synthesized with different alkylamine ligand lengths.
Linked transport behavior to structural vs energetic disorder metrics.
evidence_signal: The study reports that longer-chain ligands produce more monodisperse yet smaller nanocrystals with stronger quantum confinement and worse exciton transport, showing energetic disorder dominates the outcome.
watch_item: Improving size uniformity alone may not enhance device performance if quantum-confinement-driven energetic disorder remains high.
paper_title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
